From the start/finish straight all the way through the stadium section, the fans are packed in tight, creating a wall of noise that will spur the drivers on.

historicalReferences: Who can forget Nelson Piquet's fiery crash here in 1987? A stark reminder of the dangers of motorsport, even on a circuit like Hockenheim.
Michael Schumacher's domination at Hockenheim is legendary. The German fans remember those victories fondly, hoping for a repeat performance from the home team today.
The 2000 race saw a dramatic downpour and Rubens Barrichello's emotional victory. Weather can always play a crucial role here at Hockenheim.
In 1982, Didier Pironi suffered a career-ending crash in qualifying here. A poignant reminder of the risks these drivers take every time they get behind the wheel.
Fernando Alonso's strategic masterclass in 2012, holding off a charging Sebastian Vettel, is a Hockenheim classic. Can we expect similar tactical battles today?
The 2018 race was utter chaos with Vettel crashing out from the lead, handing the victory to Hamilton. The Hockenheimring can deliver unpredictable results.
Nigel Mansell's victory in 1992 was dominant, showcasing the power of the Williams-Renault. A golden era for Formula 1 at Hockenheim.
Ayrton Senna never won at Hockenheim. A surprising statistic for such a legendary driver. Can anyone break their own Hockenheim curse today?
The Hockenheimring has seen numerous safety car periods over the years. The long straights and challenging corners often lead to incidents.
Kimi Räikkönen's victory in 2004 was a masterclass in consistency. Can we expect a similar display of controlled speed and tyre management this year?
cornerCallouts: The drivers will need to carry good speed through Turn 1, the Nordkurve, to set themselves up for the long Parabolika straight.
Turn 2, a deceptively tricky right-hander, can easily catch drivers out, especially on cold tyres.
The hairpin at Turn 6 requires pinpoint accuracy. Get it wrong, and you'll lose valuable time in the stadium section.
Turn 8, the first part of the stadium section, is where the fans really come alive. The noise is deafening as the cars navigate this complex.
Turn 13 is a crucial overtaking opportunity, especially with DRS enabled on the run down to it.
The exit of Turn 13 is vital for a good run down the straight towards Turn 14.
Turn 16, another part of the stadium section, is a good test of car balance and driver skill.
The final corner, Turn 17, leads onto the start/finish straight. A clean exit here is essential for a quick lap time.
strategyPoints: Tyre degradation will be a key factor on this 4.574km layout, particularly with the high-speed sections and abrasive tarmac.
The pit lane length at Hockenheim is relatively short, making a one-stop strategy a viable option for some teams.
Fuel management will be crucial, especially in the early stages of the race, as the drivers push to gain positions.
With several potential overtaking opportunities, an aggressive strategy could pay dividends, but it comes with risks.
The pit window is expected to open around lap 20, but that could change depending on safety car deployments.
The long straights will put a strain on the engines. Reliability will be just as important as outright pace today.
A safety car could really mix things up, forcing teams to react quickly and adapt their strategies on the fly.
The relatively high downforce configuration will help preserve the tyres, but it could also compromise top speed on the straights.
weatherCommentary: The clouds are gathering over the Hockenheimring, and there's a real threat of rain this afternoon. That could throw a wrench into everyone's plans.
The wind is picking up, which could make the cars twitchy through the high-speed corners. The drivers will need to be extra cautious.
The track temperature is soaring, which will make tyre management even more critical. Expect to see drivers nursing their rubber throughout the race.
The humidity is high, making it tough on the drivers physically. Staying hydrated will be essential for a strong performance.
The forecast is uncertain, with a chance of showers later in the race. The teams will be keeping a close eye on the radar.
